beats.title: Hildegard Writes Ordo Virtutum
beats.description: A German abbess composed a sung morality play, one of the earliest surviving musical dramas, in which Virtues battle the Devil.
beats.note: Dated 1151, the year given by Boosey and other sources; the exact year is not documented.

beats.title: Perotin's Viderunt Omnes
beats.description: A Parisian cathedral composer wrote a four-voice setting of a Christmas chant, a landmark of polyphonic church music.
beats.note: Traditional, inferred date tied to a Paris liturgical ordinance; hedged in sources.

beats.title: Machaut's Messe de Nostre Dame
beats.description: A French poet-composer completed the first known complete polyphonic Mass setting attributed to a single composer.
beats.note: Sources say composed before 1365, probably the early 1360s; 1365 is used as the latest bound.

beats.title: Dufay's Nuper Rosarum Flores
beats.description: A Franco-Flemish composer wrote a grand motet for the consecration of a great Florentine cathedral crowned by a new dome.
beats.note: Written for the 25 March 1436 consecration of Florence Cathedral.

beats.title: Palestrina's Pope Marcellus Mass
beats.description: An Italian master of church polyphony published a Mass often said to have shown that complex choral music could keep its words clear.
beats.note: First published 1567; composition date uncertain (1555-67).

beats.title: Tallis Writes Spem in Alium
beats.description: An English composer wrote a motet for forty separate voices, arranged in eight choirs, that still thrills choral audiences.
beats.note: Composition c. 1570; scholars debate a range from the 1550s to 1573.

beats.title: Monteverdi's L'Orfeo Premieres
beats.description: An Italian court composer staged a musical drama retelling the myth of Orpheus, a founding work of opera still performed today.

beats.title: Allegri's Miserere Is Sung
beats.description: A Vatican singer-composer wrote a choral setting of a penitential psalm, later guarded as a secret of the papal chapel.
beats.note: Most often cited year; composed probably in the 1630s.

beats.title: Purcell's Dido and Aeneas
beats.description: An English composer set the tragic tale of the Carthaginian queen, ending with the aria When I Am Laid in Earth.
beats.note: 1689 is the standard date; some scholars argue for 1688 or an earlier court performance.

beats.title: Bach's Brandenburg Concertos
beats.description: A German court musician sent six richly varied concertos to a Margrave in Berlin in hopes of winning a job.
beats.note: Dedication manuscript dated 1721.

beats.title: Vivaldi Publishes The Four Seasons
beats.description: A Venetian priest-composer issued four violin concertos that paint spring, summer, autumn and winter in sound.

beats.title: Handel's Messiah Premieres
beats.description: A German-born composer in Britain unveiled his oratorio on the life of Christ, with its famous Hallelujah chorus, in Dublin.

beats.title: Gluck's Orfeo ed Euridice Premieres
beats.description: A reforming opera composer in Vienna stripped away showy vocal display in his telling of the Orpheus myth, favouring plain drama.
beats.note: Vienna version premiered 5 October 1762.

beats.title: Mozart's The Magic Flute Premieres
beats.description: A Viennese composer staged a fairy-tale opera in German, with a bird-catcher, a vengeful Queen of the Night and a magic flute.

beats.title: Haydn's The Creation Is Performed
beats.description: An aging Austrian master presented an oratorio on the Genesis story, opening with a daring orchestral depiction of chaos.
beats.note: First (private) performance 1798; first public performance 1799. Year of the first performance used.

beats.title: Rossini's The Barber of Seville
beats.description: An Italian composer's comic opera about a scheming barber and young lovers debuted in Rome to a famously rowdy reception.

beats.title: Beethoven's Ninth Premieres
beats.description: A deaf composer unveiled a symphony ending with a chorus singing the Ode to Joy, an unprecedented step for the form.

beats.title: Schubert Writes Ave Maria
beats.description: A Viennese song master set a lady's prayer from a Walter Scott poem, a melody that became one of the most beloved ever written.
beats.note: Composed 1825; published 1826.

beats.title: Berlioz's Symphonie Fantastique
beats.description: A French Romantic composer premiered a symphony telling of an artist's opium-fuelled obsession, ending in a witches' sabbath.

beats.title: Chopin Publishes His 24 Preludes
beats.description: A Polish pianist-composer issued a cycle of short piano pieces through all the keys, including the so-called Raindrop.
beats.note: Published 1839; composed 1835-39.

beats.title: Mendelssohn's Wedding March
beats.description: A German composer finished his incidental music for a Shakespeare comedy, including the march that became a bridal staple.
beats.note: Full incidental music premiered 1843 (some sources say composed 1842); the overture dates from 1826.

beats.title: Liszt's Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2
beats.description: A virtuoso pianist turned Hungarian folk tunes into a dazzling showpiece later heard in countless cartoons.
beats.note: Sketched 1847; piano version published 1851.

beats.title: Verdi's La Traviata Premieres
beats.description: An Italian composer's tragic opera of a Parisian courtesan and her doomed love opened in Venice to a cool reception.

beats.title: Strauss Premieres The Blue Danube
beats.description: A Viennese waltz king unveiled a choral waltz that became the unofficial anthem of his city's music.
beats.why_in: famous waltz by a great composer
beats.note: Premiered February 1867; composed 1866.

beats.title: Bizet's Carmen Premieres
beats.description: A French composer's opera about a fiery cigarette-factory worker and a doomed soldier shocked Paris at its opening.

beats.title: Wagner's Ring Cycle Is Staged
beats.description: A German composer presented all four parts of his epic Norse-myth opera in a theatre he had built for the purpose.
beats.note: First complete cycle, Bayreuth, 1876.

beats.title: Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake Premieres
beats.description: A Russian composer's ballet of a princess turned into a swan by a sorcerer opened at the Bolshoi to a lukewarm response.

beats.title: Rimsky-Korsakov's Scheherazade
beats.description: A Russian composer wrote a symphonic suite inspired by tales of a storyteller who kept a sultan from executing her.

beats.title: Dvorak's New World Symphony
beats.description: A Czech composer working in New York premiered a symphony inspired by American music, featuring a famous cor anglais theme.

beats.title: Puccini's La Boheme Premieres
beats.description: An Italian composer's opera of poor young artists in Paris, with a seamstress who dies of illness, opened in Turin.

beats.title: Rachmaninoff's Second Concerto
beats.description: A Russian composer-pianist premiered a lush concerto that marked his recovery from a deep depression.
beats.note: Complete premiere 1901; two movements were played in 1900.

beats.title: Debussy's Clair de Lune Published
beats.description: A French composer released a gentle piano piece named for moonlight, the best-loved movement of a suite.
beats.note: Published 1905 in Suite bergamasque; composed c. 1890.

beats.title: Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring
beats.description: A Russian composer's ballet of pagan sacrifice, with violent rhythms, provoked an uproar in the Paris audience.

beats.title: Holst's The Planets Is Performed
beats.description: An English composer's orchestral suite depicting the planets, from warlike Mars to mystical Neptune, had its first hearing in London.
beats.note: First performance 1918 (invited audience); first complete public performance 1920.

beats.title: Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue
beats.description: An American composer premiered a piece blending jazz and classical forms, opening with a famous clarinet glissando.

beats.title: Ravel's Bolero Premieres
beats.description: A French composer wrote a ballet score built on one repeating melody and a relentless snare drum, growing steadily louder.

beats.title: Prokofiev's Peter and the Wolf
beats.description: A Russian composer wrote a children's tale in which each character is played by a different instrument.
beats.why_in: famous work by a great composer

beats.title: Orff's Carmina Burana Premieres
beats.description: A German composer set medieval students' bawdy poems for chorus and orchestra, opening with the thunderous O Fortuna.

beats.title: Barber's Adagio for Strings
beats.description: An American composer's slow, aching string piece was broadcast by a famous conductor and became the sound of public mourning.

beats.title: Britten's War Requiem Premieres
beats.description: An English composer blended the Latin Mass for the dead with war poetry, for the consecration of a rebuilt cathedral.

beats.title: Glass's Einstein on the Beach
beats.description: An American minimalist composer staged a five-hour opera of repeating patterns, tied to the name of a famous physicist.

beats.title: Part Writes Spiegel im Spiegel
beats.description: An Estonian composer created a hushed piece for violin and piano of simple, bell-like notes, now a film-score favourite.

beats.title: Adams's Nixon in China Premieres
beats.description: An American composer's opera dramatised a famous diplomatic visit to Beijing, with sung roles for the leaders and their wives.
beats.note: Premiered 22 October 1987, Houston Grand Opera.
